summary: David A. Hall is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who earned his doctorate from the University of California, Berkeley in 1990 and studied under Shoshin Ichishima in 1976. He held posts at Taisho University and Montgomery College.
David Azzopardi is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied for his PhD at SOAS University of London under the doctoral supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

David B. Gray is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. from Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe, later serving at Rice University and Santa Clara University.

David Brown (1762–1812) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Joseph Milner and at Magdalene College, Cambridge. He founded the Calcutta Auxiliary Bible Society and served as Provost at Fort William College in 1800.

David Bubna-Litic is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields who completed his PhD at Western Sydney University (attested 2000). He served as a Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney.

David Burton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997). In 2010, he was attested as Senior Lecturer at Canterbury Christ Church University.

David Dean Shulman is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and earned his Ph.D. from the University of London under John Ralston Marr. He held multiple editorial and directorial posts at Hebrew University.

David Drewes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Virginia in 2006 under Karen Christina Lang. He held academic posts at Virginia, Indiana University, and the University of Manitoba.

David E. Cooper is a philosopher educated at Highgate School and St Edmund Hall. He held teaching posts at the University of Oxford, served as Professor of Philosophy at Durham University (1986–2008), and was a visiting professor at Peking University in 2022.

David E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of California, Los Angeles. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, UIUC, and the University of Hawaiʻi, and held research posts at Nichibunken and Oberlin College.

David Faure is a historian and sinologist who studied at The University of Hong Kong and Princeton University. He taught at Indiana University, St Antony's College (1990–2006), and became a director at The Chinese University of Hong Kong around 2006.

David Fiordalis is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Carleton College, the University of Chicago, and earned his doctorate from the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez, later chairing religious studies at Linfield University.

David Friedman (1903–1984) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Between circa 1950 and 1970, he served as a professor at the University of London and as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS.

David Germano is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992. He later served as Associate Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies at the University of Virginia.

David Gonsalez is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued traditional studies under teachers including Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Gordon White is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Wisconsin and Chicago, studying with Kali Charan Bahl. He taught at the University of Virginia and was J. F. Rowny Professor at UC Santa Barbara.

David J. Kalupahana (1936–2014) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Ceylon and SOAS under Stanley Weinstein and David Friedman. He taught at Ceylon before chairing the philosophy department at the University of Hawaiʻi.

David Jones is a philosopher and religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Hawaiʻi. He served as a philosophy professor in the University System of Georgia and director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

David K. Wyatt (1937–2006) was a historian who studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell University. He taught at SOAS and Michigan, chaired the history department at Cornell (1969–2002), and served as president of the Association for Asian Studies.

David Kopf (1930–2023) was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Chicago from circa 1959 to 1964. He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Minnesota from circa 1967 to 1999.
